title: Sydney Family Trip
subtitle: 27 November – 1 December 2026
tagline: Five easy days for the whole family, from our home base in Linley Point.

home.label: Where we stay
home.note: About 20–25 min drive to the city. Drive times on this page are from here and are approximate.

days.title: Harbour & first views
days.summary: Arrival day. Rest first, then free famous views at sunset (around 7:45pm).

schedule.text: Land at Sydney Airport. Immigration, bags, pick up cars.
Drive home to Linley Point (about 35–45 min). Drop bags / check in if allowed.
Late lunch near home (see "Eating near home"), then rest.
Drive to the city (about 20–25 min) and park.
Circular Quay → Opera House → Harbour Bridge views → The Rocks.
Dinner near the harbour, then drive home.

items.name: Hickson Road Reserve
items.text: Harbour Bridge framing. Stay for twilight if everyone feels up to it.

parking.heading: Where to park (all within 1 km)

options.name: Wilson car park, 155 George St
options.walk: About 300 m to Circular Quay. Closest to The Rocks dinner spots.
options.price: Night rate from ~A$24 per car (check what time the night rate starts; arriving at 5pm may cost more)
options.map: Wilson Parking 155 George Street The Rocks

options.name: Divvy, 93 Macquarie St
options.walk: About 600 m to the Opera House.
options.price: A$25 per car, Friday evening rate from 6:30pm (pre-book in the Divvy app; arriving before 6:30pm may cost more)

options.name: Opera House car park, 2A Macquarie St
options.walk: Right at the Opera House. Easiest for elders. 2.2 m height limit.
options.price: From ~A$41 per car if you leave after 7pm (prepay online)

parking.note: Sydney has no free tram or free city shuttle right now. Check the price for each car park on the day.

food.name: Pancakes on the Rocks
food.text: Family-friendly. Savoury vegetarian dishes and pancakes.
food.map: Pancakes on the Rocks The Rocks Sydney

food.name: Chat Thai
food.text: Thai stir-fries and tofu curries. Check every sauce has no seafood.

food.name: The Spice Room
food.text: Paneer, dal, naan. Over budget: set banquet for groups of 6+.

days.title: Kangaroos, koalas & outlet shopping
days.summary: Hand-feed kangaroos at Featherdale in the morning. DFO shopping in the afternoon, then Sydney-famous desserts.

schedule.text: Drive from home in both cars to Featherdale, Doonside (about 35–45 min).
Featherdale Wildlife Park. Hand-feed kangaroos and wallabies, pat a koala. Flat paths, café on site.
Drive to DFO Homebush (about 20–25 min).
DFO Homebush outlet shopping. Pick a meeting point first!
Late lunch at DFO (the food court is easiest for mixed diets).
Dinner in Glebe/Newtown, or near home, then dessert if you like.

places.heading: At Featherdale

items.name: Feed the kangaroos
items.text: Walk-through areas with kangaroos and wallabies that eat from your hand. Animal feed is sold at the park.

items.name: Koala pats
items.text: Included with entry. Stand next to a koala and pat it. NSW law does not allow holding koalas.

places.note: Open 8am–5pm every day, last entry 4pm. Adult tickets are about A$40–49. Check the price and buy online before you go.

parking.heading: Parking

options.name: DFO Homebush car park
options.price: First 2 hours free. About 4 hours (shopping + lunch): check the rate at the machine

parking.note: Money tip: the first 2 hours at DFO are free, so a car that leaves early pays nothing.

days.foodHeading: Dinner in Glebe & Newtown (about 25 min from home)

treats.name: Yo-Chi
treats.text: Self-serve frozen yoghurt, pay by weight.

treats.name: Black Star Pastry
treats.text: Famous strawberry-watermelon cake (~A$13). Contains almonds. Newtown, open till 10pm Sat.

treats.name: Hakiki
treats.text: Turkish ice cream and baklava. Enmore Rd, Newtown.

days.title: Blue Mountains
days.summary: The big day: cable cars, rainforest and the Three Sisters.

schedule.text: Leave home in both cars. About 1¾–2 hours drive.
Scenic World: Skyway, Cableway, short rainforest boardwalk.
Late lunch in Katoomba (book ahead for 10+).
Echo Point: Three Sisters photos.
Drive home. Dinner only if wanted.

places.heading: Don't miss

items.name: Scenic Skyway
items.text: Cable car across the valley, with a glass floor section.

places.note: The Scenic Railway is very steep. Skip it unless each person wants to go.

parking.heading: Parking & tickets

options.name: Scenic World car park, 1 Violet St
options.walk: At the entrance. 2 m height limit.

options.name: Echo Point car park
options.walk: Next to the lookout. 5 accessible bays.
options.price: Paid (council pay-by-app). Check the sign for the rate

parking.note: Book Scenic World ahead for a ~12:30pm session (from A$64 per adult; Sunday may cost more).

food.name: Station Bar
food.text: Best fit. Wood-fired veg pizzas. Open 7 days.

food.name: Basil Nut
food.text: Asian fusion, vegan options. Tight: Sunday lunch ends 3:30pm. Call ahead for 10+.

food.name: Pho Moi
food.text: Vietnamese noodles. Check the broth is vegetarian and Sunday hours.

food.name: 8Things
food.text: Global street food. Closes about 3pm Sunday, so likely too late after Scenic World.

days.title: Bondi Beach & giraffes
days.summary: Two ways to do today. Pick one the night before.

items.name: Taronga Giraffe Encounter
items.text: Daily at 10:40am. A$39.95 covers up to 4 people. Zoo entry is extra (about A$50–55 per adult).

items.name: Icebergs viewpoint
items.text: Famous ocean pool with waves crashing in.

items.name: Bondi to Tamarama path (optional)
items.text: Cliffs and surf. Elders can stay at the cafés.

parking.heading: Where to park

options.name: Free streets in North Bondi
options.walk: Blair St, Hastings Pde, Wairoa Ave. About 5–10 min walk (500–800 m).
options.price: Free, but mostly 2–4 hour limits. We stay about 6 hours, so cars must move once. Read every sign

options.name: Queen Elizabeth Drive (beachfront meters)
options.walk: Right behind the beach. Accessible bays near the Pavilion.
options.price: ~A$12.40/hour per car (7am–7pm), pay by plate. A full day is about A$75 per car

options.name: Park & ride: Westfield Bondi Junction
options.walk: Then bus 333 or 380 to Campbell Parade (about 10–15 min).
options.price: 2 hours free (4 hours on weekdays for free Westfield members). Bus fares for 10+ people add up, so check the total

options.name: Taronga Zoo car park
options.walk: Bradleys Head Road, at the top entrance.
options.price: About A$18–24 per day per car. Check the machine
options.map: Taronga Zoo car park Bradleys Head Road

parking.note: Easiest plan: drop elders at the Pavilion, then park on the free streets.

food.name: Bondi Trattoria
food.text: Top pick. Monday risotto special A$27, veg pasta and pizza. Book for the group.

food.name: Bondi Pizza Gallery
food.text: Vegetarian pizzas. Check hours and seats for 10+.

food.name: Funky Pies
food.text: Vegan pies. Takeaway backup, not for a sit-down group.

items.name: Option A: Giraffes for two, Bondi for all
items.who: Two of us go to Taronga Zoo for the morning. Everyone else does Bondi. We all meet for lunch. Uses both cars.

schedule.text: Zoo pair: drive to Taronga Zoo (about 15–20 min). Park on Bradleys Head Road.
Zoo opens. Buy the Giraffe Encounter at the Top Plaza shop (from 9am) or in the Taronga app.
Feed the giraffes, with the harbour behind them. Then see the koalas and kangaroos.
Zoo pair: drive to Bondi (about 35–45 min).
Family: Leave home (about 35–45 min). Drop elders at Bondi Pavilion, then park.
Bondi Beach walk, Pavilion and beach photos.
Bondi Icebergs viewpoint. Relax at a café. Fitter guests can walk part of the coast path.
Late lunch near the beach.
Relax, last photos, drive home.
Optional dinner near home.

items.name: Option B: Everyone to Taronga Zoo
items.who: Whole family goes to the zoo instead of Bondi. Big harbour views, lots of Australian animals.

schedule.text: Leave home in both cars (about 15–20 min). Park on Bradleys Head Road.
Zoo opens. Buy Giraffe Encounter tickets at the Top Plaza shop. One ticket covers up to 4 people.
Giraffe feeding. Then koalas, kangaroos and the harbour lookouts at an easy pace.
Late lunch at the zoo cafés, or in Mosman. Check vegetarian options and ask about seafood.
Last animals, then drive home and rest.
Optional dinner near home.

items.note: The zoo is on a steep hill. The Sky Safari cable car is closed while a new one is built, so elders should keep to the top half and take breaks.

days.title: On to Newcastle
days.summary: Check out. Family takes the train from Central. Sujay & Laura drive with the luggage. Meet in Newcastle.

schedule.text: Breakfast, pack, check out.
Sujay & Laura drive the family to Sydney Central Station in a few trips (about 25 min each way). Or the family takes public transport (use the trip planner below).
Sujay & Laura drive to Newcastle with as much of the luggage as possible (about 2 hours).
Family catches a CCN train to Newcastle (check times on the day).
Family arrives at Newcastle Interchange. Sujay & Laura pick up.
Late lunch in Newcastle. Bring vegetarian snacks for the train.

days.timesNote: Tuesday times are a rough guide. They depend on how many trips the car needs.

items.name: Newcastle Interchange
items.text: Toilets, lifts and a taxi rank.

train.heading: Train steps for the family
steps: Arrive at Sydney Central 20–30 min before the train.
Find the Central Coast & Newcastle Line (CCN) intercity train.
Tap on with an Opal card or contactless bank card. No booking needed.
Check the train sign says Newcastle (some trains stop earlier). The ride is about 2½–3 hours.

nearHome.heading: Eating near home
nearHome.intro: For easy lunches and dinners close to Linley Point. Call ahead to check hours and seats for 10+.

items.name: Lane 198, Gladesville
items.text: Asian dishes with vegetarian and vegan options. Books out: reserve early.

items.name: Mount Everest Indian & Nepalese, Hunters Hill
items.text: Curries, dal and momos. Good for groups.
items.map: Mount Everest Indian Nepalese Restaurant Hunters Hill

items.name: Chat Thai, Chatswood
items.text: Thai noodles and tofu curries. Check every sauce has no seafood.

footer: Prices and opening hours were checked in November 2026 and can change. Food photos show the kind of dish, not the restaurant's own food.
